probes.question: In the Wug Test, what plural shows a child has inferred the basic rule?
True or false: in the Wug Test, the target words are made-up words that the child cannot have heard before.

image.alt: Two friendly round teal cartoon creatures with big eyes and a little tuft, one larger and one smaller, standing side by side.

panels.text: A child is shown a simple picture of a fanciful creature with a nonsense name: “This is a WUG. Now there is another one. There are two of them. There are two ____.”
Each target word was a made-up but plausible-sounding pseudoword, so the child cannot have heard it before.
A child who answers “wugs” has apparently inferred, perhaps unconsciously, the basic rule for forming plurals.
Jean Berko Gleason's major finding: even very young children are able to connect suitable endings to nonsense words they have never heard before.
